Addressing complexity and variability in B2B product design: When designing the B2B product, we faced challenges due to the complex internal business logic and numerous intersection points of the system. The package status and features evolve at each stage of the delivery process, leading to variations in the appearance of package cards. This complexity underscores the importance of thoroughly considering edge cases to ensure accurate data processing across all scenarios.

Adjust designs based on language, culture, devices, and user habits: The focus on localization emphasized adapting to regional culture and user habits, particularly in Japan, where our team's understanding of local preferences and language nuances was initially limited. Throughout the design process, we consulted local experts and actively engaged with Japanese users to learn about typical user behaviors and adjusted our designs to match Japanese device specifications and text styles. This thorough localization process ensured that our design met the specific requirements of the Japanese market, making the product more effective and user-friendly.

Propose design assumptions and drive the design process in the face of business uncertainty:

During the internal and external meetings, we refined our design processes and guided clients to articulate their new requirements, some of which were initially undiscovered and emerged as the project progressed. This often led to new requirements with many uncertainties related to business operations. We needed to propose various assumptions and develop multiple design scenarios to determine which options were most effective. Looking forward, we hope to support these design assumptions with more user-centric data, enhancing the reliability and effectiveness of our design solutions.
